proof.text: Frobenius is natural on characteristic-$p$ schemes: for every scheme map $a:U\to T$, its maps on sections satisfy $a^\sharp(f^{p^b})=a^\sharp(f)^{p^b}$, and both Frobenius maps are identities on underlying spaces. Thus $aF_U^b=F_T^ba$ by [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. The field map $x\mapsto x^{p^b}$ on $k$ is injective, since $(x-y)^{p^b}=0$ implies $x=y$, and surjective, since $t^{p^b}-c$ has a root in the algebraically closed field $k$. Hence $\delta=F_s^b$ is an automorphism, including $\delta=1$ for $b=0$. In particular $F_X^bz=z\delta$ and $F_V^bv=v\delta$ for every geometric lift $v:s\to V$.

proof.text: First work with a sheaf $M$ on a characteristic-$p$ scheme $T$. Put $P=(F_T^b)^*$, $Q=(F_T^b)_*$ and $B(V)=V\times_{T,F_T^b}T$. By [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback], $R_V=(F_V^b,h):V\to B(V)$ is the specified natural isomorphism for each weakly etale $h:V\to T$. Thus the specified direct-image trivialization is $d_M:QM\to M$, with $d_M(V)=M(R_V)$. Let $\eta:M\to QPM$ be the unit of the module adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $(L_1,R_1)=(P,Q)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$, and right-adjoint comparison $d^{-1}$. The adjoint trivialization in the statement is characterized by $Q(\tau_M)\eta_M=d_M^{-1}$. Evaluated at $V$, this says that the pullback-unit section $\eta_{M,V}(a)\in PM(B(V))$ is sent by $\tau_M$ to $M(R_V^{-1})(a)\in M(B(V))$. The coefficient identification preserves constant sections by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], so these are $A$-linear section maps with no scalar factor.

source.place: Tag 0F6W, lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale; agent deduction of the specified adjoint trivialization on represented germs

proof.text: Take a geometric point $u:s\to T$ and a germ $[V,v,a]\in M_{F_T^bu}$, so $hv=F_T^bu=u\delta$. By the inverse formula in [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence], $c_{F_T^b,u,M}^{-1}$ represents this germ by the pullback-unit section of $PM$ on $B(V)$ at the lift $w=(v,u)$. We use the order $V\times_TT$ here; swapping the factors in the cited comparison keeps these two projections. Step 1 gives $h(v\delta^{-1})=u$ and $F_V^b(v\delta^{-1})=v$, hence $R_V(v\delta^{-1})=(v,u)=w$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and invertibility of $R_V$ give $R_V^{-1}w=v\delta^{-1}$. Step 2 therefore sends the germ to $[B(V),w,M(R_V^{-1})(a)]$. The pointed morphism $R_V^{-1}:(B(V),w)\to(V,v\delta^{-1})$ identifies this with $[V,v\delta^{-1},a]$ by the defining germ relation in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk].

proof.text: For any scheme automorphism $\beta$ of $s$, precomposition sends a pointed neighbourhood $(V,v)$ of $u$ to $(V,v\beta)$ of $u\beta$, leaving site arrows and sections unchanged. A relation $[V',v',a']=[V,v,M(e)(a')]$ with $ev=v'$ remains a relation because $e(v\beta)=v'\beta$. Thus [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] defines $r_{u,\beta,M}$ on the quotient, with inverse $r_{u\beta,\beta^{-1},M}$. The maps preserve sums and $A$-multiplication: the same pointed common refinement and the same section operations can be precomposed with $\beta$. For a sheaf map $f:M\to M'$, both orders send $[V,v,a]$ to $[V,v\beta,f_V(a)]$, so $r$ is natural. In Step 3 the resulting map is exactly $r_{u\delta,\delta^{-1},M}$.

proof.text: Specialize Step 3 to $T=s$, $u=\mathrm{id}_s$ and $M=N$. It gives the first formula $[V,v,a]\mapsto[V,v\delta^{-1},a]$ under $c_{\delta,\mathrm{id}_s,N}$. Specialize it to $T=X$, $u=z$ and $M=H$; since $F_X^bz=z\delta$, it gives $(\tau_X^{(b)}{}_H)_z\,c_{F_X^b,z,H}^{-1}=r_{z\delta,\delta^{-1},H}$. These are equalities of maps, since every germ has a representative in the colimit of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Step 4 proves naturality of the right side; naturality of the left side is also part of [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] and of the specified natural transformation [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback].

proof.text: Apply the pullback naturality statement of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] to $z:s\to X$. With its specified composition comparison $C:Lz^*L(F_X^b)^*\to L\delta^*Lz^*$, it gives $\tau_s^{(b)}{}_{Lz^*H}\circ C_H=Lz^*(\tau_X^{(b)}{}_H)$. Take the stalk at $\mathrm{id}_s$. The composition equation for $c$ in [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] identifies the two source stalks with $H_{F_X^bz}=H_{z\delta}$. Its reparametrization equation, applied to $t=z$, $u=\delta$ and the field automorphism inducing $\delta^{-1}$, reads $r_{z\delta,\delta^{-1},H}c_{z,\delta,H}=c_{z,\mathrm{id}_s,H}r_{\delta,\delta^{-1},Lz^*H}$. Thus it identifies the target maps from Steps 3--5 as well. This proves the asserted compatibility through the specified composition comparisons; it does not replace those comparisons by arbitrary isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply Steps 2--6 in every degree of a bounded complex. All section maps commute with the differentials by their naturality, so the displayed germ equations are equalities of chain maps. The module pullbacks are exact and their derived pullbacks are the termwise functors by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The cited Frobenius trivialization is the termwise one by [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback], and [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] supplies the stalk comparisons, composition equalities and reparametrizations after localization. Consequently these chain maps give the specified maps in the ordinary derived categories. Parts (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] carry their naturality and equalities to the localization. No resolution choice changes the formula. For $b=0$, $R_V$, $\delta$, and both germ reparametrizations are identities, consistent with $\tau^{(0)}=1$.

title: Normalization of the absolute-Frobenius stalk trivialization
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $X$ a scheme of characteristic $p$, and $z:s\to X$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and use small pro-etale sites, constant $A$-module sheaves and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $F_X,F_s$ for absolute $p$-power Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. For $b\geq0$, put $\delta=F_s^b$, an automorphism, and let $\tau_T^{(b)}:L(F_T^b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ for $T=X,s$ be the specified relative-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback]. Thus its normalization is given by the relative Frobenius isomorphisms $(F_V^b,h):V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\times_{T,F_T^b}T$ for weakly etale $h:V\to T$, and the adjoint inverse-image identification.

For a bounded $A_s$-module complex $N$, under the canonical stalk comparison $(L\delta^*N)_{\mathrm{id}_s}\cong N_\delta$ of [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence], the map $(\tau_s^{(b)}{}_N)_{\mathrm{id}_s}$ sends every termwise represented germ $[V,v,a]\in N_\delta$ [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk], with $h:V\to s$ weakly etale and $hv=\delta$, to
$$[V,v\delta^{-1},a]\in N_{\mathrm{id}_s}.$$
For a bounded $A_X$-module complex $H$, write $r_{u,\beta,H}:H_u\to H_{u\beta}$ for the isomorphism induced by $[V,v,a]\mapsto[V,v\beta,a]$, where $u:s\to X$ and $\beta$ is a scheme automorphism of $s$. Using the comparisons $c$ of [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] and $F_X^bz=z\delta$, one has
$$(\tau_X^{(b)}{}_H)_z\circ c_{F_X^b,z,H}^{-1}=r_{z\delta,\delta^{-1},H}:H_{z\delta}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_z.$$
The formulas are natural in $H$ and compatible with pullback along $z$ through the composition comparisons; they are formulas for the specified trivialization and remain valid after derived localization.
